findings.title: Uncertainty whether coaching content fits new technical practice group
findings.description: When told the incoming fall practice group is a data-and-analytics team (more technical, younger) rather than management consultants, Nadia acknowledged the account hadn't considered whether the coaching content would suit a more technical audience. No specific defect or missing capability was named; Sam (internal) proposed tuning coach-matching for tech-leadership backgrounds as a proactive service action, and the customer did not push a concrete product change.
findings.quote: That's a thoughtful catch. We hadn't thought about whether the coaching would fit a more technical crowd.
findings.severity_reason: No concrete defect or feature gap identified; it's a forward-looking consideration being handled operationally, not a product change request.
findings.match_note: No catalogue issue covers coach-matching tuning; this is an internally-initiated service action, not a customer-raised product bug/feature.

findings.title: Customer wants existing onboarding-with-coaching process applied to new seat cohort
findings.description: Desmond asked that the new ~40-50 person practice group joining in the fall receive the same onboarding-with-coaching approach used previously, from day one. This is a request to apply an already-existing, working service/process to newly purchased seats as part of the renewal expansion, not a defect in or missing capability of the BetterBark product itself.
findings.quote: The onboarding-with-coaching approach worked so well the first time, I want the new group to have it immediately.
findings.severity_reason: Commercial/onboarding scope request, not a product defect or feature gap; already resolved by the seat-expansion decision made later in the call.
findings.match_note: No matching product issue; this is a services/rollout request tied to the seat expansion, not a software bug or feature.

findings.title: Customer requests written rate-delta breakdown for finance approval
findings.description: Nadia asked Sam to send a written breakdown of the rate difference between building the 50 new seats into the renewal versus adding them mid-term, so she can present the math to her finance partner. This is a request for a commercial/pricing document to support internal approval, not a BetterBark product defect or feature.
findings.quote: And send me the rate-delta breakdown so I can show my finance partner the math on the expansion.
findings.severity_reason: Pure pricing/commercial documentation request; no product functionality involved.
findings.match_note: Not a product issue; pricing/quote documentation requests fall outside the product catalogue entirely.

findings.title: General exhortation to maintain coaching quality, no specific complaint
findings.description: Desmond stated that the renewal depends on coaching quality staying high and that he'd notice if it ever became transactional. No specific defect, feature gap, or incident was cited — it's a general expectation-setting statement tied to renewal, not an actionable product report.
findings.quote: Just keep the quality up. The day it feels transactional, I'll notice.
findings.severity_reason: General sentiment with no specific, actionable detail for an engineer or product team to address.
findings.match_note: Too vague to map to any catalogue issue; no concrete symptom, location, or reproduction given.
